concerns.text: The research question asks whether digital decluttering *causally* improves cognition and well‑being, yet the plan implements a within‑subject pre/post design with no control or randomization. Practice effects on SART and Ospan (known to improve with repeated exposure) are not ruled out, so the design cannot support a causal inference.

Digital‑use compliance is measured solely via self‑reported daily logs. Self‑report is prone to social desirability and recall bias, threatening construct validity of the ‘intervention fidelity’ variable.

Monte‑Carlo simulations estimate power ≈ 0.58 for a medium effect (d = 0.5) with the planned N ≈ 34–50. This is well below the conventional 0.80 threshold, making the study under‑powered to detect the effects it claims to test.

No strategies are described to control for confounds such as test‑retest learning, time‑of‑day effects, or participant attrition beyond simple exclusion. Without a control group or counterbalancing, these confounds can bias the observed change scores.
